name: maxmin_char_double
expr: mx = max('abc'); mn = min('abc'); [v, idx] = max('abc'); cm = max(M); rd = max(M, [], 2); al = max('abc', [], 'all'); mo = double(mode('abc'));
comment: max/min of a CHAR array return DOUBLE (the code point), NOT char — MATLAB does not preserve the char class for max/min (mode DOES keep char). max('abc')=99, min('abc')=97, [v,idx]=max -> 99/3, column-wise max(['abc';'xyz'])=[120 121 122], dim2=[99 122], 'all'=99, mode('abc')='a' (double()=97). NOTE: the binary max('a','c') form is NOT tested here — MATLAB ERRORS on it ('Invalid second argument'); numkit is lenient (returns 99 double) but that is not a MATLAB-matched form. The ; inside ['abc';'xyz'] is a matrix-row separator. bugs/builtin/maxmin-char-double.md.
